title: Parity: capability-table overflow policy diverges - Python refuses non-egress at regular-tail limit (5.03), Rust evicts LRU non-egress and admits
description: Found by worker-1 while fixing project-LICHEN-worker6-hdb3 (bead project-LICHEN-worker6-zhgy-style parity call). Python CapabilityTable.record (python/src/lichen/coap/resources/capability_announce.py:99-107): when len(entries) >= capacity - egress_reservation, a non-egress insert is REFUSED (returns False -> resource responds 5.03); only egress-sourced inserts may LRU-evict. Rust CapabilityTable::insert (rust/lichen-gateway/src/capability.rs:86-97): a new non-egress insert with the regular partition full EVICTS the LRU non-egress entry and ADMITS (returns true); insert returns false only when the table is at 256 and evict_lru(false) finds no non-egress victim (all-egress table), or on a refresh that clears the egress bit with regular full. Consequence: under announcement flood the Python gateway sheds non-egress capabilities (5.03, keeps its existing cache stable), the Rust gateway keeps admitting by evicting older ones (cache churn; combined with fawm the replay floor of an evicted gateway is lost). Both are self-consistent and unit-tested locally; pick ONE policy for the spec (spec 8.12/8.11 does not pin the overflow behavior): likely Rust aligns to Python's refuse-with-5.03 (throttles churn, preserves floors, matches the shipped Python resource), or Python adopts evict-and-admit. Also decide the dispatch response on refusal (Python 5.03) and pin it with cross-suite tests. The Rust hdb3 fix (resources.rs propagate insert() bool -> 5.03 on refusal + capability_announce_rejects_recover_and_table_full_is_503 test) pins the Rust refusal path regardless.
